questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the hydrocarbon but-1-en-3-yne ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$):
Statement I: The carbon atoms in but-1-en-3-yne exhibit $\text{sp}$ and $\text{sp}^2$ hybridisation states only.
Statement II: The molecule contains a total of seven $\sigma$-bonds and three $\pi$-bonds.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write down the expanded structural formula of but-1-en-3-yne: $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{H}$.
Step 2: Determine the hybridisation of each carbon atom. Carbon-1 ($\text{CH}_2=$) is $\text{sp}^2$, Carbon-2 ($=\text{CH}-$) is $\text{sp}^2$, Carbon-3 ($-\text{C}\equiv$) is $\text{sp}$, and Carbon-4 ($\equiv\text{CH}$) is $\text{sp}$. Therefore, only $\text{sp}$ and $\text{sp}^2$ hybridisation states are present in the molecule, confirming Statement I.
Step 3: Count the number of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds. There are two $\text{C}-\text{H}$ $\sigma$-bonds at C1, one $\text{C}=\text{C}$ $\sigma$-bond between C1 and C2, one $\text{C}-\text{H}$ $\sigma$-bond at C2, one $\text{C}-\text{C}$ single $\sigma$-bond between C2 and C3, one $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ $\sigma$-bond between C3 and C4, and one $\text{C}-\text{H}$ $\sigma$-bond at C4, giving $2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 7$ $\sigma$-bonds. The double bond contributes one $\pi$-bond and the triple bond contributes two $\pi$-bonds, giving $1 + 2 = 3$ $\pi$-bonds. Hence, both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond length in ethyne ($\text{HC}\equiv\text{CH}$) is significantly shorter than the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond length in ethene ($\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2$) and ethane ($\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_3$).
Reason (R): With increasing s-character of the carbon hybrid orbital, the electrons of the orbital are held more closely to the carbon nucleus, decreasing bond length and increasing electronegativity.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the hybridisation of carbon in each compound. In ethane, carbon is $\text{sp}^3$ ($25\%$ s-character); in ethene, carbon is $\text{sp}^2$ ($33.3\%$ s-character); in ethyne, carbon is $\text{sp}$ ($50\%$ s-character).
Step 2: Evaluate the physical consequence of higher s-character. Since spherical s-orbitals penetrate closer to the nucleus than p-orbitals, hybrid orbitals with greater s-character hold shared bonding electrons closer to the nucleus, causing the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond length to decrease in the order: ethane ($111\text{ pm}$) > ethene ($108.7\text{ pm}$) > ethyne ($106\text{ pm}$).
Step 3: Relate Assertion and Reason. The reason directly explains why the $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond in ethyne is the shortest among the three hydrocarbons. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II to identify the structural classification of organic compounds:
List I (Compound):
A. Tetrahydrofuran
B. Tropolone
C. Naphthalene
D. Cyclobutane
List II (Classification):
I. Alicyclic hydrocarbon
II. Benzenoid aromatic compound
III. Non-benzenoid aromatic compound
IV. Heterocyclic non-aromatic compound
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
C) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
D) A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Classify compound A (Tetrahydrofuran). Tetrahydrofuran is a five-membered saturated ring containing four carbon atoms and one oxygen atom in the ring; it is non-aromatic and contains a heteroatom, so it is a heterocyclic non-aromatic compound (A matches IV).
Step 2: Classify compound B (Tropolone). Tropolone contains a seven-membered planar conjugated ring with alternating single and double bonds obeying Huckel's $(4n+2)\pi$ rule ($6\pi$ electrons), but does not contain a benzene ring; hence it is a non-benzenoid aromatic compound (B matches III).
Step 3: Classify compound C (Naphthalene) and D (Cyclobutane). Naphthalene contains fused benzene rings, making it a benzenoid aromatic compound (C matches II). Cyclobutane is a saturated cyclic ring of carbon atoms, classified as an alicyclic hydrocarbon (D matches I). Thus, the correct matching sequence is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

questions.questionText:
What is the correct IUPAC name of the branched alkane having the following condensed structure:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$?
options: A) 3-ethyl-5-methylhexane
B) 2-methyl-4-ethylhexane
C) 4-ethyl-2-methylhexane
D) 2,4-diethylpentane
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the longest continuous carbon chain. Expanding the ethyl group at position 4 gives $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$. Tracing from left to right gives a 6-carbon chain (hexane). Selecting the ethyl branch as chain terminus also gives 6 carbons, so hexane is the principal chain.
Step 2: Number the carbon chain from both ends to obtain the lowest locant set. Numbering from left to right gives substituents at carbons 2 and 4 (locant set: $2, 4$). Numbering from right to left gives substituents at carbons 3 and 5 (locant set: $3, 5$). By the lowest locant rule, numbering from left to right is preferred.
Step 3: Alphabetize the substituent names. The substituents are 'ethyl' at position 4 and 'methyl' at position 2. Because 'ethyl' precedes 'methyl' alphabetically, the prefix order is 4-ethyl-2-methyl. Thus, the IUPAC name is 4-ethyl-2-methylhexane.

questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding IUPAC nomenclature of unsaturated hydrocarbons:
Statement I: When both a double bond and a triple bond are equidistant from the two ends of an acyclic carbon chain, the double bond is given the lower locant number.
Statement II: According to IUPAC rules, the systematic name for $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$ is pent-4-en-1-yne.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. IUPAC rule states that if a double bond and a triple bond are present at symmetrical positions from the two terminal carbon atoms, the carbon chain is numbered giving preference (lower locant) to the double bond. Thus, Statement I is fully correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II for $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. The double bond is at position 1 from the right end, and the triple bond is at position 1 from the left end. Following the priority rule, numbering must begin from the double bond: C1 is $=\text{CH}_2$, C2 is $-\text{CH}=$, C3 is $-\text{CH}_2-$, C4 is $-\text{C}\equiv$, and C5 is $\equiv\text{CH}$.
Step 3: Construct the IUPAC name. The 5-carbon alk-en-yne chain is numbered $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$, giving pent-1-en-4-yne. Therefore, pent-4-en-1-yne is incorrect. Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.questionText: What is the systematic IUPAC name of the polyfunctional carboxylic acid represented by the formula $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$?
options: A) 2-oxopentanoic acid
B) 4-oxopentanoic acid
C) 4-ketopentan-1-oic acid
D) 2-carboxybutan-3-one
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the principal functional group according to IUPAC priority rules. Between the carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$) and the ketone group ($>\text{C}=\text{O}$), the carboxylic acid has higher priority and serves as the principal functional group with the suffix '-oic acid'.
Step 2: Number the longest carbon chain containing the principal functional group starting with the carboxylic acid carbon as C1: $\text{C}_1\text{OOH}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_2-\text{C}_3\text{H}_2-\text{C}_4\text{O}-\text{C}_5\text{H}_3$.
Step 3: Name the substituent. The carbonyl oxygen at C4 acts as a secondary functional group and is designated by the prefix 'oxo'. With a five-carbon saturated chain, the parent name is pentanoic acid. Thus, the IUPAC name is 4-oxopentanoic acid.

questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Methoxypropane ($\text{CH}_3-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) and ethoxyethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) are metamers of each other.
Reason (R): Metamerism arises due to the presence of different alkyl chains attached to the same polyvalent functional group on either side.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Check the molecular formulas of both compounds. Methoxypropane has the formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ and ethoxyethane also has the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. Both share the same ether functional group ($-O-$).
Step 2: Examine the alkyl groups attached to the ether oxygen. In methoxypropane, the alkyl groups are methyl ($\text{CH}_3-$) and propyl ($-\text{C}_3\text{H}_7$). In ethoxyethane, both alkyl groups are ethyl ($-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$).
Step 3: Evaluate Assertion and Reason. Because the compounds have the same molecular formula and functional group but differ in the distribution of carbon atoms on either side of the divalent oxygen atom, they are metamers. Reason (R) accurately defines metamerism and provides the exact explanation for Assertion (A).

questions.questionText:
Consider the following pairs of organic compounds:
(i) Propan-1-ol and Propan-2-ol
(ii) Ethoxyethane and Butan-1-ol
(iii) Propanal and Propan-2-one
(iv) Propanoic acid and Methyl ethanoate
Which of the above pairs represent functional group isomerism?
options: A) (i) and (ii) only
B) (i), (ii), and (iii) only
C) (ii) and (iv) only
D) (ii), (iii), and (iv) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze pair (i). Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol both possess the alcohol ($-OH$) functional group but differ in the position of the $-OH$ group on the 3-carbon chain (C1 vs C2); thus, they are position isomers, not functional isomers.
Step 2: Analyze pair (ii). Ethoxyethane (an ether, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) and butan-1-ol (an alcohol, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) share identical molecular formulas but belong to different homologous series/functional groups; thus, they are functional isomers.
Step 3: Analyze pairs (iii) and (iv). Propanal (an aldehyde, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$) and propan-2-one (a ketone, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$) are functional isomers. Propanoic acid (a carboxylic acid, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) and methyl ethanoate (an ester, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$) are functional isomers. Therefore, pairs (ii), (iii), and (iv) exhibit functional group isomerism.

questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding covalent bond cleavage and reaction intermediates:
Statement I: Heterolytic cleavage of a neutral covalent bond results in an unequal distribution of shared electrons, yielding one cation and one anion.
Statement II: In a methyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3^+$), the central carbon atom is $\text{sp}^2$ hybridised with a vacant, unhybridised p-orbital perpendicular to the trigonal planar molecular plane.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In heterolytic fission, the shared electron pair is retained entirely by one of the bonded atoms (the more electronegative one), forming a negatively charged anion and leaving the other atom positively charged as a cation. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. In the methyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3^+$), carbon forms three $\sigma$-bonds with three hydrogen atoms using three $\text{sp}^2$ hybrid orbitals with $120^\circ$ bond angles in a trigonal planar geometry. The remaining sixth valence electron is lost, leaving an empty $2p_z$ orbital perpendicular to the molecular plane. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of both statements. Both Statement I and Statement II are scientifically correct statements according to NCERT.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of electron-withdrawing inductive ($-I$) effect of substituents according to NCERT?
options: A) $-\text{COOH} > -\text{NO}_2 > -\text{CN} > -\text{F} > -\text{OH}$
B) $-\text{NO}_2 > -\text{CN} > -\text{COOH} > -\text{F} > -\text{Cl}$
C) $-\text{F} > -\text{Cl} > -\text{NO}_2 > -\text{CN} > -\text{COOH}$
D) $-\text{CN} > -\text{NO}_2 > -\text{F} > -\text{COOH} > -\text{OH}$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the standard NCERT series for the relative strength of the electron-withdrawing inductive ($-I$) effect.
Step 2: The order of $-I$ effect is determined by electronegativity and the presence of formal positive charges or polar multiple bonds: $-\text{NO}_2 > -\text{CN} > -\text{COOH} > -\text{F} > -\text{Cl} > -\text{Br} > -\text{I} > -\text{OH} > -\text{OCH}_3 > -\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$.
Step 3: Verify the options against this established NCERT series. The nitro group ($-\text{NO}_2$) has the strongest $-I$ effect due to the formal positive charge on nitrogen and two electronegative oxygens, followed by cyano ($-\text{CN}$), carboxyl ($-\text{COOH}$), fluorine ($-\text{F}$), and chlorine ($-\text{Cl}$). Thus, the order $-\text{NO}_2 > -\text{CN} > -\text{COOH} > -\text{F} > -\text{Cl}$ is correct.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The electromeric effect is a temporary electron displacement effect that occurs only at the requirement of an attacking reagent.
Reason (R): When the attacking reagent is removed from the reaction sphere, the shifted $\pi$-electron pair returns to its original position restoring the initial state.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Define the electromeric effect. The electromeric effect is defined as the complete transfer of a shared pair of $\pi$-electrons to one of the atoms joined by a multiple bond on the demand of an attacking reagent.
Step 2: Contrast permanent and temporary effects. Inductive and resonance effects are permanent because they exist in the resting molecule in the ground state. In contrast, the electromeric effect operates solely when an electrophile or nucleophile approaches the substrate.
Step 3: Connect Assertion and Reason. If the reagent is withdrawn or removed before reaction completes, the $\pi$-electrons revert immediately to their resting orbital positions. This complete reversibility upon reagent removal is the exact reason why the electromeric effect is classified as temporary. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding canonical resonance structures of organic molecules:
Statement I: All canonical contributing structures of a resonance hybrid must have identical positions of atomic nuclei and the same number of paired and unpaired electrons.
Statement II: A resonance contributing structure possessing like charges on adjacent carbon atoms contributes maximally to the stability of the resonance hybrid.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I against resonance criteria. In resonance structures, the arrangement of nuclei must remain strictly identical; only electrons ($\pi$-electrons and lone pairs) change positions. Furthermore, the total number of paired and unpaired electrons must be conserved in all contributing structures. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II against electrostatic rules of resonance. According to stability rules of canonical forms, like charges situated on adjacent atoms create severe electrostatic repulsion and significantly raise the potential energy. Consequently, such structures are extremely unstable and contribute negligibly to the resonance hybrid.
Step 3: Conclude the correctness of the statements. Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II describing fundamental electron displacement effects in organic chemistry:
List I (Electronic Effect):
A. Inductive effect
B. Resonance effect
C. Hyperconjugation
D. Electromeric effect
List II (Characteristic Mechanism):
I. Delocalization of $\sigma_{\text{C}-\text{H}}$ electrons into an adjacent empty p-orbital or $\pi$-system
II. Complete transfer of a shared pair of $\pi$-electrons to an atom under the influence of an attacking reagent
III. Permanent polarization of $\sigma$-bonds transmitted along a carbon chain due to electronegativity difference
IV. Delocalization of $\pi$-electrons or lone pairs across conjugated p-orbitals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
C) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
D) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match Inductive effect (A). The inductive effect involves the permanent shift of $\sigma$-electrons along a saturated carbon chain caused by electronegativity differences between bonded atoms (A matches III).
Step 2: Match Resonance effect (B). The resonance (mesomeric) effect involves delocalization of $\pi$-electrons or lone pairs through overlapping conjugated p-orbitals (B matches IV).
Step 3: Match Hyperconjugation (C) and Electromeric effect (D). Hyperconjugation involves the interaction of electrons in a $\sigma$-bond (primarily $\text{C}-\text{H}$) with an adjacent unshared p-orbital or $\pi$-orbital (C matches I). The electromeric effect is a temporary complete shift of a $\pi$-electron pair in the presence of an attacking reagent (D matches II). Thus, the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText: Which of the following alkyl carbocations possesses the maximum number of $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms capable of participating in hyperconjugation, resulting in highest thermodynamic stability?
options: A) Ethyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^+$)
B) tert-Butyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$)
C) Isopropyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^+$)
D) Methyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3^+$)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Count the number of $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms attached to carbons directly adjacent to the positively charged carbocation center in each species.
Step 2: In methyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3^+$), there are zero $\alpha$-hydrogens ($0$ hyperconjugative structures). In ethyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^+$), there is one methyl group giving $3$ $\alpha$-hydrogens. In isopropyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^+$), there are two methyl groups giving $6$ $\alpha$-hydrogens. In tert-butyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$), there are three methyl groups providing $9$ $\alpha$-hydrogens.
Step 3: Relate hyperconjugation to stability. Greater number of $\alpha$-hydrogens allows more hyperconjugative (no-bond resonance) contributing structures, dispersing the positive charge over a larger volume and maximizing thermodynamic stability. Therefore, the tert-butyl carbocation has the maximum stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The ethynyl carbanion ($\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}^-$) is significantly more stable than the ethenyl carbanion ($\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}^-$) and the ethyl carbanion ($\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2^-$).
Reason (R): The unshared electron pair in ethynyl carbanion resides in an $\text{sp}$ hybrid orbital with $50\%$ s-character, where electrons are held most tightly by the positive nucleus compared to $\text{sp}^2$ and $\text{sp}^3$ orbitals.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the hybridisation of the negatively charged carbon atom in each carbanion. In $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}^-$, the anionic carbon is $\text{sp}$ hybridised; in $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}^-$, it is $\text{sp}^2$; in $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2^-$, it is $\text{sp}^3$.
Step 2: Relate s-character to electronegativity and anion stability. The percentage of s-character is $50\%$ for $\text{sp}$, $33.3\%$ for $\text{sp}^2$, and $25\%$ for $\text{sp}^3$. Orbitals with greater s-character are more compact and closer to the positive nucleus, making the carbon more electronegative and significantly better able to stabilize negative charge.
Step 3: Evaluate Assertion and Reason. The stability order $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}^- > \text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}^- > \text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2^-$ is directly explained by the variation in s-character of the carbon hybrid orbital holding the lone pair. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II to identify the most suitable separation technique for each mixture of compounds:
List I (Mixture/Compound):
A. Camphor and Sodium chloride
B. Chloroform (b.p. $334\text{ K}$) and Aniline (b.p. $457\text{ K}$)
C. Crude petroleum fractions
D. Aniline and water mixture
List II (Purification Method):
I. Steam distillation
II. Sublimation
III. Fractional distillation
IV. Simple distillation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
B) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
C) A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match mixture A (Camphor + NaCl). Camphor undergoes sublimation directly from solid to vapor upon heating, whereas sodium chloride is non-volatile; hence sublimation separates them (A matches II).
Step 2: Match mixture B (Chloroform + Aniline). Chloroform has a boiling point of $334\text{ K}$ and aniline boils at $457\text{ K}$. Since their boiling points differ by more than $25\text{ K}$ ($123\text{ K}$ difference) and both liquids do not decompose, simple distillation is used (B matches IV).
Step 3: Match mixture C (Crude petroleum) and D (Aniline + water). Crude petroleum contains fractions with closely spaced boiling points ($< 25\text{ K}$ difference), requiring fractional distillation (C matches III). Aniline is steam volatile and practically immiscible with water, making steam distillation the ideal separation method (D matches I). Thus, the correct sequence is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the purification of organic compounds by steam distillation:
Statement I: Steam distillation is applied to separate liquids that are completely miscible with water at all temperatures.
Statement II: In steam distillation, the mixture boils at a temperature significantly higher than the normal boiling points of both water and the organic liquid.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Steam distillation is specifically employed for substances that are steam volatile and practically insoluble or completely immiscible with water (such as aniline or nitrobenzene). If a liquid is completely miscible with water (like ethanol or acetone), steam distillation cannot be used. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the mixture boils when the total vapor pressure ($P_{\text{total}} = p_{\text{water}} + p_{\text{organic}}$) equals atmospheric pressure ($1\text{ atm}$). Because the total vapor pressure is the sum of two positive vapor pressures, the required boiling pressure of $1\text{ atm}$ is reached at a temperature lower than $373\text{ K}$ ($100^\circ\text{C}$), which is lower than the boiling points of both pure water and the organic liquid. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.
Step 3: Conclude overall validity. Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText: In a thin-layer chromatography (TLC) experiment using a silica gel plate, the developing solvent front migrated a distance of $8.0\text{ cm}$ from the baseline. An organic component formed a distinct spot that traveled a distance of $3.2\text{ cm}$ from the baseline. What is the retardation factor ($R_f$) of this organic compound?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Recall the definition and formula for the retardation factor ($R_f$) in chromatography.
Step 2: The retardation factor is defined as the ratio of the distance moved by the substance from the baseline to the distance moved by the solvent front from the baseline: $R_f = \frac{\text{Distance traveled by compound}}{\text{Distance traveled by solvent front}}$.
Step 3: Substitute the measured experimental values: $R_f = \frac{3.2\text{ cm}}{8.0\text{ cm}} = 0.40$. The value of $R_f$ is always dimensionless and less than or equal to $1.0$. Thus, the retardation factor is $0.40$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): When an organic compound containing hydrogen is heated with dry copper(II) oxide ($\text{CuO}$), the formation of water is confirmed by the appearance of a blue color upon contact with anhydrous copper(II) sulfate.
Reason (R): Anhydrous copper(II) sulfate is white in color and absorbs liberated water to form hydrated copper(II) sulfate ($\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$), which has a characteristic blue color.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false
D) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the chemical reaction occurring during the qualitative test for hydrogen. When an organic compound is heated with $\text{CuO}$, hydrogen is oxidized to water according to the reaction: $2\text{H} + \text{CuO} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Cu} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Step 2: Examine the detection of liberated water. The water vapor passes over white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate ($\text{CuSO}_4$). Water molecules coordinate to $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions forming pentahydrate crystals: $\text{CuSO}_4 + 5\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Crystal field splitting in the hydrated complex causes d-d transitions resulting in an intense blue color.
Step 3: Evaluate Assertion and Reason. The formation of the blue pentahydrate directly explains why anhydrous copper(II) sulfate turns blue and confirms the presence of hydrogen. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding Lassaigne's test for the qualitative detection of elements:
Statement I: In Lassaigne's test, organic compounds are fused with metallic sodium to convert covalently bonded nitrogen, sulfur, and halogens into water-soluble ionic sodium salts.
Statement II: Hydrazine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{NH}_2$) gives a characteristic Prussian blue coloration in Lassaigne's test for nitrogen.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. The elements nitrogen, sulfur, and halogens are covalently bound in organic molecules. Fusing with molten sodium metal converts them into ionic salts: $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \rightarrow \text{NaCN}$, $2\text{Na} + \text{S} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{S}$, and $\text{Na} + \text{X} \rightarrow \text{NaX}$, which dissolve readily in water. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. For nitrogen detection, the formation of cyanide ions ($\text{CN}^-$) requires both carbon and nitrogen from the organic compound ($\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \rightarrow \text{NaCN}$). Hydrazine ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{NH}_2$) contains nitrogen but no carbon; on heating with sodium, it decomposes into $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{N}_2$ without forming $\text{NaCN}$. Thus, hydrazine does not give Prussian blue in Lassaigne's test.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of the statements. Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText: When sodium fusion extract containing sulfur is treated with sodium nitroprusside solution, a characteristic purple-violet coloration is observed. What is the chemical formula of the coordination complex responsible for this purple color?
options: A) $\text{Na}_2[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]$
B) $\text{Na}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$
C) $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$
D) $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the species present in the Lassaigne's extract when sulfur is present. Fusing sulfur with metallic sodium yields ionic sodium sulfide: $2\text{Na} + \text{S} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{S}$.
Step 2: Write the reaction with sodium nitroprusside. Sodium nitroprusside has the chemical formula $\text{Na}_2[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]$. When sulfide ions ($\text{S}^{2-}$) react with the nitroprusside complex in aqueous solution, the sulfide coordinates with the nitrosyl ligand: $\text{Na}_2\text{S} + \text{Na}_2[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}] \rightarrow \text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$.
Step 3: Confirm the formula and color. The resulting complex, sodium thionitroprusside ($\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$), imparts an intense violet-purple coloration, confirming the presence of sulfur in the organic compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the detection of halogens in Lassaigne's extract:
Statement I: Prior to testing for halogens using silver nitrate solution, the sodium fusion extract is acidified with concentrated hydrochloric acid.
Statement II: Boiling the extract with dilute nitric acid decomposes any sodium cyanide and sodium sulfide present into volatile hydrogen cyanide and hydrogen sulfide gases, preventing false positive precipitates.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Lassaigne's extract must NEVER be acidified with hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$) because $\text{HCl}$ itself introduces chloride ions, which react with silver nitrate ($\text{AgNO}_3$) to form an insoluble white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$, creating a false-positive test for halogens. Dilute nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$) is used instead. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. If nitrogen or sulfur is present in the compound, the fusion extract contains $\text{NaCN}$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$. If $\text{AgNO}_3$ is added directly without boiling with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$, silver ions form white $\text{AgCN}$ or black $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$ precipitates that interfere with halogen detection. Boiling with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ decomposes them: $\text{NaCN} + \text{HNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{NaNO}_3 + \text{HCN}\uparrow$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{S} + 2\text{HNO}_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{NaNO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of the statements. Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText: What is the systematic IUPAC name of the polyfunctional organic compound having the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$?
options: A) 5-hydroxy-3-oxohexanoic acid
B) 2-hydroxy-4-oxohexanoic acid
C) 3-oxo-5-hydroxyhexanoic acid
D) 5-hydroxy-3-ketohexan-1-oic acid
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the principal functional group using IUPAC seniority priority order: $-\text{COOH} > >\text{C}=\text{O} > -\text{OH}$. The carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$) has highest priority and gives the suffix '-oic acid'.
Step 2: Number the continuous parent carbon chain containing the principal functional group, assigning C1 to the carboxyl carbon: $\text{C}_1\text{OOH}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_2-\text{C}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_4\text{H}_2-\text{C}_5\text{H}(\text{OH})-\text{C}_6\text{H}_3$. The parent chain has 6 carbon atoms (hexanoic acid).
Step 3: Name and alphabetize the substituents. At carbon-5 there is a hydroxyl group designated by prefix 'hydroxy', and at carbon-3 there is a carbonyl oxygen designated by prefix 'oxo'. Arranging alphabetically ('h' precedes 'o') gives 5-hydroxy-3-oxohexanoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the correct IUPAC name for the naturally occurring flavoring compound vanillin, whose structural formula features a benzene ring with an aldehyde group at C1, a methoxy group at C3, and a hydroxyl group at C4?
options: A) 3-methoxy-4-hydroxybenzaldehyde
B) 4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde
C) 1-formyl-3-methoxy-4-hydroxybenzene
D) 2-methoxy-4-formylphenol
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify the principal functional group attached directly to the benzene ring. Comparing $-\text{CHO}$, $-\text{OH}$, and $-\text{OCH}_3$, the aldehyde group ($-\text{CHO}$) has the highest seniority and defines the parent compound as benzaldehyde, with the formyl-bearing carbon designated as C1.
Step 2: Number the ring substituents to yield the lowest locant set: numbering towards the substituents gives C3 for the methoxy group ($-\text{OCH}_3$) and C4 for the hydroxyl group ($-OH$).
Step 3: Alphabetize substituent prefixes. The prefix 'hydroxy' begins with 'h' and 'methoxy' begins with 'm'. Because 'h' precedes 'm' alphabetically, 'hydroxy' is written before 'methoxy'. Combining with locants gives 4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding tautomerism in $\beta$-dicarbonyl compounds:
Statement I: In pure liquid state or in non-polar solvents, pentane-2,4-dione exists predominantly in its enol form ($>75\%$ enol content) rather than its keto form.
Statement II: The exceptional stability of the enol tautomer of pentane-2,4-dione is governed by resonance conjugation between the double bond and carbonyl group, reinforced by a strong six-membered intramolecular hydrogen-bonded chelate ring.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. While simple monocarbonyls like acetone exist almost exclusively in the keto form ($>99.9\%$) at equilibrium, $\beta$-diketones such as pentane-2,4-dione (acetylacetone) exhibit very high enol content ($76\%$ in pure liquid and $>90\%$ in hexane/gas phase). Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The enol tautomer (4-hydroxypent-3-en-2-one) forms a planar conjugated system ($-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{OH})-$) with extended $\pi$-electron delocalization. This geometry allows the enolic $-\text{OH}$ hydrogen to form a strong intramolecular hydrogen bond with the carbonyl oxygen, completing an extraordinarily stable pseudo-aromatic six-membered ring (chelation). Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of both statements. Both Statement I and Statement II are scientifically correct statements according to NCERT.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): trans-But-2-ene has a significantly higher melting point than cis-but-2-ene, but cis-but-2-ene has a higher boiling point than trans-but-2-ene.
Reason (R): trans-But-2-ene possesses centrosymmetric geometry allowing closer packing in the crystal lattice, whereas cis-but-2-ene has a permanent dipole moment giving rise to stronger intermolecular dipole-dipole attractions in the liquid state.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze boiling points of cis and trans isomers. In cis-but-2-ene, the two methyl group bond dipoles reinforce each other, yielding a net molecular dipole moment ($\mu = 0.33\text{ D}$). In trans-but-2-ene, the opposing bond dipoles cancel out symmetrically ($\mu = 0\text{ D}$). Greater dipole-dipole attractions in cis-but-2-ene elevate its boiling point ($277\text{ K}$) above that of trans-but-2-ene ($274\text{ K}$).
Step 2: Analyze melting points. Melting point depends primarily on how efficiently molecules pack into a crystal lattice. The linear, centrosymmetric trans-isomer packs much more symmetrically and tightly into the solid lattice than the bent, U-shaped cis-isomer, making the melting point of trans-but-2-ene ($167\text{ K}$) higher than that of cis-but-2-ene ($134\text{ K}$).
Step 3: Evaluate Assertion and Reason. The explanation of symmetry for lattice packing (melting point) and dipole moment for liquid cohesion (boiling point) is fully sound. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding stereoisomerism in tartaric acid:
Statement I: meso-Tartaric acid contains two asymmetric (chiral) carbon atoms but fails to rotate plane-polarized light, being completely optically inactive.
Statement II: The optical inactivity of meso-tartaric acid is caused by external compensation between equal concentrations of dextrorotatory and laevorotatory enantiomers.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Tartaric acid, $\text{HOOC}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{COOH}$, possesses two chiral centers at C2 and C3. In the meso isomer, the molecule is achiral and optically inactive despite the presence of chiral centers. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Optical inactivity of meso compounds arises from internal compensation: the molecule contains an internal plane of symmetry ($\sigma$), such that the optical rotation produced by one half of the molecule is exactly cancelled by the equal and opposite rotation of the other half within the same molecule. External compensation refers to a $1:1$ equimolar mixture of separate enantiomers (a racemic mixture), not a meso compound. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of both statements. Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding enantiomers and diastereomers:
(i) Enantiomers possess identical melting points, boiling points, and solubilities in achiral solvents, but rotate plane-polarized light in equal and opposite directions.
(ii) Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other and exhibit different physical constants such as melting points, boiling points, and dipole moments.
(iii) A racemic modification ($50\%$ (+)-isomer and $50\%$ (-)-isomer) has zero net optical rotation due to external compensation.
(iv) A pair of diastereomers can be separated by conventional physical techniques such as fractional distillation or crystallization, whereas a pair of enantiomers cannot be separated by ordinary fractional distillation.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (i) and (ii) only
B) (i), (ii), and (iii) only
C) (ii), (iii), and (iv) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (i). Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images. In an achiral environment, all intermolecular forces are identical, leading to identical scalar physical properties (b.p., m.p., density, solubility), while their specific optical rotations have identical magnitude but opposite signs. Thus, statement (i) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (ii). Diastereomers have different spatial relationships between atoms without being mirror images; hence they possess distinct scalar physical constants (different energies, dipole moments, densities, melting points). Thus, statement (ii) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (iii) and (iv). A racemic mixture contains equal numbers of $(+)$ and $(-)$ enantiomer molecules, so the optical rotation of one enantiomer is externally compensated by the other. Because diastereomers have different boiling points and solubilities, they are readily separable by fractional distillation or fractional crystallization, whereas enantiomers require chiral resolving agents or chromatography on a chiral stationary phase. Thus, all four statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II to identify the electronic influence of substituents directly attached to a conjugated benzene ring:
List I (Substituent):
A. $-\text{OCH}_3$
B. $-\text{NO}_2$
C. $-\text{Cl}$
D. $-\text{CHO}$
List II (Electronic Effect and Directing Nature):
I. Strong $-M$ and $-I$ effects; deactivating and meta-directing
II. $+M$ effect with stronger $-I$ effect; overall deactivating but ortho/para-directing
III. $+M$ effect dominating over $-I$ effect; activating and ortho/para-directing
IV. Moderate $-M$ and $-I$ effects through carbonyl $\pi$-conjugation; deactivating and meta-directing
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
B) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
C) A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
D) A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match substituent A ($-\text{OCH}_3$). The methoxy group donates its unshared electron pair into the aromatic ring via $+M$ resonance, which outweighs its $-I$ inductive withdrawal, activating the ring towards electrophilic attack and directing incoming groups to ortho/para positions (A matches III).
Step 2: Match substituent B ($-\text{NO}_2$). The nitro group possesses a formal positive charge on nitrogen and two electronegative oxygens, exerting exceptionally strong $-M$ and $-I$ electron-withdrawing effects, deactivating the ring and directing meta (B matches I).
Step 3: Match substituent C ($-\text{Cl}$) and D ($-\text{CHO}$). Halogens like chlorine exhibit a unique anomaly: electron withdrawal by inductive effect ($-I$) is stronger than electron release by resonance ($+M$), causing net deactivation, but resonance still directs substitution to ortho and para positions (C matches II). The formyl group ($-\text{CHO}$) withdraws electron density by resonance ($-M$) through its polar carbonyl group, deactivating the ring and directing meta (D matches IV). Thus, the correct sequence is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The magnitude of heat of hydrogenation ($\Delta H_{\text{hydro}}$) of trans-but-2-ene is lower than that of cis-but-2-ene and but-1-ene.
Reason (R): trans-But-2-ene has six hyperconjugative $\alpha$-hydrogens with negligible steric repulsion between methyl groups, making it thermodynamically more stable than cis-but-2-ene and but-1-ene.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Relate alkene stability to heat of hydrogenation. Hydrogenation of isomeric alkenes produces the same alkane (butane). Since more stable alkenes sit in a lower potential energy well, they release less heat upon catalytic hydrogenation (lower magnitude of $\Delta H_{\text{hydro}}$).
Step 2: Compare thermodynamic stabilities of the isomers. But-1-ene has only two $\alpha$-hydrogens (less hyperconjugation), giving the highest heat of hydrogenation ($-127\text{ kJ/mol}$). Both cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene have six $\alpha$-hydrogens, but cis-but-2-ene suffers from steric van der Waals repulsion between the two eclipsing methyl groups on the same side of the double bond ($-120\text{ kJ/mol}$).
Step 3: Evaluate Assertion and Reason. trans-But-2-ene minimizes steric strain with methyl groups located on opposite sides, releasing the least heat of hydrogenation ($-115\text{ kJ/mol}$). Thermodynamic stability directly accounts for the lower heat of hydrogenation. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText: Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of thermodynamic stability for the given carbon-centered free radicals?
options: A) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\dot{\text{C}} > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > (\text{CH}_3)_2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H} > \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$
B) $\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 > (\text{CH}_3)_2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\dot{\text{C}} > \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$
C) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > (\text{CH}_3)_3\dot{\text{C}} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H} > \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$
D) \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > (\text{CH}_3)_2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\dot{\text{C}} > \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze resonance stabilization in radicals. The benzyl free radical ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$) has extensive resonance delocalization over the entire aromatic $\pi$-system (four contributing canonical structures), providing the greatest stabilization energy.
Step 2: Analyze allylic and alkyl radicals. The allyl radical ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$) is stabilized by two equivalent resonance structures. Resonance stabilization provides greater stabilization than hyperconjugation alone.
Step 3: Analyze alkyl free radical stability. Among alkyl radicals, stabilization is provided by hyperconjugation with $\alpha$-hydrogens: tert-butyl ($9$ $\alpha$-H) > isopropyl ($6$ $\alpha$-H) > methyl ($0$ $\alpha$-H). Combining resonance and hyperconjugation gives the decreasing stability order: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 > (\text{CH}_3)_3\dot{\text{C}} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H} > \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II to identify the characteristic chemical classification of various reactive species:
List I (Reagent/Species):
A. Cyanide ion ($^-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$)
B. Nitronium ion ($\text{NO}_2^+$)
C. Sulfur trioxide ($\text{SO}_3$)
D. Triethylamine ($(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N}$)
List II (Classification):
I. Positively charged electrophile active in aromatic substitution
II. Ambident nucleophile capable of attacking through carbon or nitrogen
III. Neutral Lewis base nucleophile possessing a non-bonding electron pair
IV. Neutral electrophile containing an electron-deficient sulfur center
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
D) A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Classify species A ($^-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$). The cyanide ion possesses unshared electron pairs on both carbon and nitrogen, allowing it to coordinate through carbon (yielding nitriles) or nitrogen (yielding isonitriles); thus it is an ambident nucleophile (A matches II).
Step 2: Classify species B ($\text{NO}_2^+$). The nitronium ion bears a positive charge on nitrogen and acts as the reactive electrophile in aromatic nitration reactions (B matches I).
Step 3: Classify species C ($\text{SO}_3$) and D ($(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N}$). In sulfur trioxide, sulfur is bonded to three electronegative oxygen atoms via polar double bonds, creating a highly electron-deficient central sulfur atom that behaves as a neutral electrophile (C matches IV). Triethylamine has a nitrogen atom with an unshared lone pair that can be donated to an electrophile, functioning as a neutral Lewis base nucleophile (D matches III). Thus, the correct sequence is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding distillation under reduced pressure:
Statement I: Glycerol can be purified readily by simple distillation at standard atmospheric pressure ($760\text{ mm Hg}$) without experiencing thermal breakdown.
Statement II: Distillation under reduced pressure is employed for liquids having high boiling points that tend to decompose at or below their normal boiling temperatures.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Glycerol has a normal boiling point of $563\text{ K}$ ($290^\circ\text{C}$) at $760\text{ mm Hg}$. When heated toward this temperature under normal pressure, it undergoes extensive thermal decomposition into acrolein and other degradation products before it can boil. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. By lowering the external pressure above the liquid surface (e.g., using a vacuum pump to $12\text{ mm Hg}$), the liquid boils when its vapor pressure equals this reduced pressure ($453\text{ K}$ for glycerol). Boiling occurs at a much lower temperature where thermal decomposition is entirely avoided. This is the exact principle and application of vacuum distillation. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of the statements. Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Paper chromatography is classified fundamentally as partition chromatography rather than adsorption chromatography.
Reason (R): In paper chromatography, water molecules trapped within the cellulose fibers of the paper act as the stationary liquid phase, and separation occurs via continuous differential partitioning of components between this stationary phase and the mobile liquid solvent.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the classification of chromatographic techniques. Column chromatography and thin-layer chromatography (TLC) utilize solid adsorbents (silica gel or alumina) and operate primarily on differential adsorption. In contrast, paper chromatography operates on the principle of liquid-liquid partition.
Step 2: Examine the physical mechanism of paper chromatography. Filter paper contains cellulose chains that strongly bind approximately $6\%$ to $8\%$ water by mass. This bound water forms an immobilized liquid film acting as the stationary phase. As the mobile organic solvent migrates up the paper via capillary action, solutes distribute themselves between the mobile liquid phase and the stationary aqueous phase according to their partition coefficients.
Step 3: Evaluate Assertion and Reason. The continuous partitioning between the bound water layer and the moving solvent is the precise scientific reason why paper chromatography is categorized as partition chromatography. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the chemical reactions involved in Lassaigne's test for nitrogen:
Statement I: When sodium fusion extract containing sodium cyanide is heated with iron(II) sulfate in alkaline medium, sodium hexacyanoferrate(II) ($\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$) is formed.
Statement II: On acidifying the reaction mixture with concentrated sulfuric acid, some $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions are oxidized to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, which react with hexacyanoferrate(II) to form a Prussian blue precipitate of $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Trace the initial reaction of Lassaigne's nitrogen test. Sodium cyanide present in the extract reacts with freshly prepared iron(II) sulfate in alkaline medium: $6\text{NaCN} + \text{FeSO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6] + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$. This produces sodium hexacyanoferrate(II). Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Trace the acidification and color development step. When acidified with concentrated sulfuric acid and heated, atmospheric oxygen or trace oxidants in acid medium convert some $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ into $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions. These ferric ions then react with hexacyanoferrate(II) anions: $4\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} + x\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}\downarrow$ (ferric ferrocyanide / Prussian blue). Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of the statements. Both Statement I and Statement II are scientifically correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the qualitative detection of an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulfur:
Statement I: When an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulfur is fused with sodium, sodium thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) is formed, giving a blood-red coloration of $[\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$ upon treatment with $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions.
Statement II: If sodium is taken in excess during fusion, sodium thiocyanate decomposes into sodium cyanide and sodium sulfide, and Prussian blue color is formed instead of a blood-red coloration upon performing the nitrogen test.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. When both N and S are present, sodium fusion produces sodium thiocyanate: $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} + \text{S} \rightarrow \text{NaSCN}$. Addition of acidified ferric chloride yields a blood-red complex $[\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$ (or $\text{Fe(SCN)}_3$) due to iron(III) thiocyanate: $\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{SCN}^- \rightarrow [\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$. No Prussian blue is formed here because free $\text{CN}^-$ ions are absent. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. When sodium metal is fused in excess, the excess sodium reduces sodium thiocyanate into separate sodium cyanide and sodium sulfide: $\text{NaSCN} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{NaCN} + \text{Na}_2\text{S}$. With free cyanide ions now available, the standard Prussian blue precipitate forms during the iron(II) sulfate test. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclude the validity of both statements. Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
